name: Scribe
subcategory: screen recording, walkthroughs and product demos
tagline: Capture a browser workflow and produce editable step-by-step documentation

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited guides; browser capture; link sharing and embeds; 1-week version history; no desktop capture

tiers.name: Pro Personal
tiers.limits: 1+ paid seat; desktop and browser capture; advanced export, editing and branding
tiers.notes: The supplied snapshot said $29/month; the live rate is $35 monthly or $25/month annually.

tiers.name: Pro Team
tiers.limits: Minimum 5 paid seats; team collaboration and management
tiers.notes: Minimum spend is $85/month monthly or $65/month equivalent on annual billing.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats, security, administration, analytics and support

pricing.freeTierCaps: unlimited guides, browser capture, links/embeds and 1-week version history; no desktop capture
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (about 20% lower); plans apply to the whole team
pricing.hiddenCosts: Pro Team requires at least 5 paid seats; a workspace cannot mix free and paid members, so upgrading the team upgrades every billable user.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Scribe, capture a browser workflow and produce editable step-by-step documentation. The hard boundary is automatic capture quality, redaction, team libraries, integrations, and sharing, plus capture polish, hosting, and collaboration.
coreLoopDIY: Capture a browser workflow, annotate key steps, and produce editable step-by-step documentation the user can export and share.
whatYouLose: automatic capture quality, redaction, team libraries, integrations, and sharing
ongoingBurden: OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Scribe because the recording itself is easy; the subscription removes upload, transcoding, sharing, organization, and support work. The recurring cost buys OS permissions, codecs, rendering performance, uploads, storage, links, and viewer analytics, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Cap
priorArt.desc: Open-source screen recording and sharing product with modern desktop architecture.

alternatives.name: Mimik
alternatives.desc: Scribe without the cloud: click through a workflow and get local, editable steps.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Folge
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A proper desktop guide maker whose free forever ends at guide number six.

rejectedAlternatives.name: MotionShot
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Two watermarked guides, then the free story is over.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro Personal plan and a personal desktop recorder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Scribe in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, ffmpeg, and SQLite; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture a browser workflow, annotate key steps, and produce editable step-by-step documentation the user can export and share.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Offer screen, window, or region capture plus optional microphone audio.
Show an always-visible recording timer and make stop available from the tray.
Create a non-destructive trim view with crop, zoom, cursor highlight, and text callouts.
Render locally through ffmpeg with sensible H.264 and WebM presets.
Generate a poster frame, transcript, and Markdown summary beside each video.
Provide copy-file-path and reveal-in-folder actions instead of mandatory cloud upload.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public cloud hosting.
Deliberately leave out viewer identity and engagement analytics.
Deliberately leave out enterprise workspaces and SSO.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
